title: Montréal
intro: Walk and talk, browse beautiful little shops, eat very well, and linger over coffee and dessert. One relaxed route each day, with nearby extras when you feel like it.

hotel.name: Alt Hotel Montréal
hotel.label: Booked
hotel.description: Your booked base in Griffintown, at Peel and Wellington, near Chez Potier and the Lachine Canal.

booking: Hotel booked: Alt Hotel Montréal, 120 Rue Peel, Griffintown. Restaurant reservations, skating tickets, Notre-Dame admission, and flights remain pending unless booked separately.
assumptions: Flying via YUL. Friday arrival around midnight. Sunday: Milo lands in New York by 10 PM; Forrest can get home to Boston later. Selected flight options land at LGA 9:30 PM and BOS 9:28 PM. All times Eastern. Alt Hotel Montréal is booked. Flights and activities remain pending.

places.name: La Banquise
places.description: The flexible late-arrival poutine stop. Keep it casual tonight and save the nice meal for Saturday.
places.note: Check late kitchen hours before leaving the hotel.

places.name: St-Viateur Bagel
places.description: The original wood-fired bagel shop. Get a hot sesame bagel and watch the baking.
places.note: Original flagship at 263 Saint-Viateur West: published hours daily 6 AM–midnight. Counter-service bakery; no reservation.

places.name: Café Olimpico
places.description: Espresso and a lively neighborhood crowd. Pause here together after bagels rather than treating coffee as another quick errand.
places.note: Use the original Saint-Viateur location.

places.name: Bref
places.description: A bright gallery-boutique of ceramics, prints, and limited-edition design objects.
places.note: Saturday and Sunday 11 AM–5 PM on the contact page.

places.name: LVNEA
places.description: Locally made botanical perfumes: resins, woods, unusual atmospheric scents.
places.note: Entrance on Casgrain; published weekend hours 11 AM–6 PM.

places.name: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly
places.mapQuery: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly, 176 Rue Bernard Ouest
places.description: Art books, graphic novels, and good things to pick up and show each other.
places.note: On Bernard, by Bref and the record shops.

places.name: H Parfums
places.description: A polished niche-perfume boutique with independent houses to compare.
places.note: Saturday 10 AM–5 PM; Sunday noon–5 PM.

places.name: Schwartz’s Deli
places.description: Montréal smoked meat, mustard, and a pickle. Order medium-fat.
places.note: Use takeaway if the sit-down queue is long.

places.name: Habitat 67
places.description: A genuinely unusual stacked-housing experiment. A guided visit has more substance than a distant glance.
places.note: The 2026 tour calendar reaches Nov 22. Saturday slots are unverified; internal access requires a tour. Separate taxi trip across the water.

places.name: L’Express
places.description: A classic French bistro with a serious cellar and late service.
places.note: Reservations for two available online through Libro; larger parties by phone. Saturday check showed only midnight slots, not a 7 PM table.

places.name: Cloakroom Bar
places.mapQuery: Cloakroom Bar, 2175 Rue de la Montagne
places.description: An intimate, no-menu cocktail bar that builds a drink around the flavors you like.
places.note: 25 seats, no reservations. Ask the price before ordering rare spirits.

places.name: Crew Collective & Café
places.description: A spectacular former bank turned café. A proper place to sit, have coffee, and talk while enjoying the architecture.
places.note: A public café, not just coworking space. Tables can be busy; seating is not guaranteed.

places.name: Place d’Armes & Notre-Dame
places.description: The blue-and-gold basilica interior is much more striking than a quick look at the façade.
places.note: Daytime adult entry starts at CAD 16 + tax; AURA starts at CAD 37 + tax. Sunday sightseeing is 12:30–4 PM.

places.name: L’Empreinte coopérative
places.description: Québec-made ceramics, glass, jewelry, and artisan objects in an actual makers’ cooperative.
places.note: 88 Saint-Paul Est. Confirm seasonal November opening times.

places.name: Rue Saint-Paul → Old Port
places.description: Stone streets, river views, little passages, and a long waterfront promenade.
places.note: The exposed river edge is windy; the streets are an easy shorter loop.

places.name: Olive et Gourmando
places.mapQuery: Olive et Gourmando, 351 Rue Saint-Paul Ouest
places.description: A cozy old-city café for excellent sandwiches, baked goods, and a proper lunch.
places.note: 351 Saint-Paul Ouest; published weekends 8 AM–5 PM. Takeaway avoids a brunch wait.

places.name: Leméac
places.description: A more polished Outremont bistro for a long lunch or proper dinner.
places.note: Weekend brunch/lunch 10 AM–3 PM; dinner 5–11 PM. Reserve.

places.name: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann
places.mapQuery: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann, 316 Avenue du Mont-Royal Est
places.description: A slice of caramelized, buttery kouign-amann. Split one while it is warm.
places.note: Saturday option. Tastet lists Sunday closed.

places.name: North Star Machines à Piastres
places.mapQuery: North Star Machines à Piastres, 3908 Boulevard Saint-Laurent
places.description: Vintage pinball, a drink, and a little friendly competition.
places.note: Opposite the Schwartz’s stretch; machine noise, not a quiet lounge. Confirm hours.

places.name: Bota Bota
places.description: A floating hot-and-cold spa with river views. Keep this as an optional spa outing if you specifically want a quiet session.
places.note: Silence is required on the boat, so this is a weaker fit for a conversation-focused afternoon. Confirm conversation-permitted areas before booking. Swimsuit needed.

places.name: Cité Mémoire night walk
places.description: Local stories projected onto real buildings after dark. Try a couple on an evening walk.
places.note: Operator lists reopened scenes Wednesday–Sunday after nightfall. Check the current app map.

places.name: Ex-Voto
places.description: A well-curated mix of local clothing, ceramics, stationery, and home objects.
places.note: Pair with État de choc; both sit on the Saint-Laurent approach to Little Italy.

places.name: Bernie Beigne
places.description: Big, fluffy doughnuts and playful flavors. The fun sweet stop in this cluster.
places.note: Bernard Ouest. Check current hours and go before sell-outs.

places.name: Les chocolats de Chloé
places.mapQuery: Les chocolats de Chloé, 546 Avenue Duluth Est
places.description: Handmade chocolates, caramels, and crunchy chocolate-coated sponge toffee.
places.note: 546 Duluth Est; Saturday 11 AM–6 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: Monarque · Brasserie
places.description: The upgraded dinner pick: a handsome room, polished service, and ambitious French cooking.
places.note: Book the brasserie, not the separate four-course dining room. Saturday service from 5 PM.

places.name: Chez Potier
places.description: The refined pastry stop: individual cakes, chocolate work, macarons, and beautiful seasonal desserts.
places.note: 630 Wellington; weekends 8 AM–5 PM. Excellent for pastries, but seating is limited: this is not the main long café break.

places.name: Bar George
places.description: Carved wood, stained glass, cocktails, and a grand mansion setting. Get a drink and the café gourmand.
places.note: The current menu lists five mini desserts for CAD 20. Bar seating is walk-in.

places.name: Ratafia
places.description: Inventive plated desserts with wine or cocktails. This is the dessert destination, not just a bakery stop.
places.note: Evening only, Tuesday–Saturday from 5 PM; closed Sunday. It replaces the evening plan, not a quick daytime detour.

places.name: État de choc
places.description: Bean-to-bar chocolates, tasting bars, and gifts that are actually worth bringing home.
places.note: 6466 Saint-Laurent; Saturday 10 AM–5 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: Atrium Le 1000 · indoor skating
places.mapQuery: Atrium Le 1000, 1000 Rue De La Gauchetière Ouest
places.description: A year-round indoor rink beneath a glass atrium, downtown and north of your Griffintown hotel.
places.note: Official Sunday hours 11:30 AM–6 PM. Timed-arrival tickets are recommended; availability is not guaranteed.

places.name: MONOKIINI · ceramics & café
places.description: Handmade ceramics, a café, and makers working in the studio.
places.note: Boutique visit and coffee, not a booked workshop.

places.name: atelier b · workshop boutique
places.description: Locally made natural-fiber clothing plus jewelry, ceramics, and other makers’ work, with the workshop behind the shop.
places.note: Saturday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: WACHIYA · Cree artisan objects
places.description: Authentic Cree beadwork, jewelry, sculpture, and handmade objects from Eeyou Istchee.
places.note: 79 Saint-Paul East, opposite L’Empreinte. Published listings show Wednesday–Sunday 10 AM–6 PM.

places.name: Galerie Noël Guyomarc’h
places.description: Contemporary art jewelry and sculptural objects by independent makers. A more unusual browse than a conventional luxury jeweler.
places.note: Published Saturday hours 11 AM–5 PM; closed Sunday. Images are archive gallery photographs, not current inventory.

days.label: Friday night
days.title: Late flight. Straight to the hotel.
days.summary: Leave work around 7 PM and expect arrival around midnight. Tonight is just arrival and sleep.

blocks.title: Alt Hotel Montréal · late check-in
blocks.text: After landing, take a taxi to your booked Alt Hotel Montréal at 120 Rue Peel in Griffintown. Tell reception you expect arrival after midnight. Eat before the flight. The reservation should include Friday night even if you check in early Saturday.

days.label: Saturday
days.title: Northern makers, then skating and a proper dinner.
days.summary: One trip north for Bref, perfume, lunch, chocolate, and MONOKIINI. Back downtown once for skating, Monarque, and an optional cocktail.

blocks.title: St-Viateur → Olimpico · start strong
blocks.text: Taxi to the original St-Viateur bakery at 263 Saint-Viateur West. Get warm sesame bagels and watch the wood-fired oven, then walk east to Olimpico for espresso and a proper sit-down. This is the planned start, not an optional detour.

nearby.text: Bernie Beigne, 23 Bernard West: big, freshly made doughnuts if you want a second breakfast treat. A short neighborhood detour; buy one to share and keep room for lunch.
The independent bookshop on Bernard is an easy browse as you move toward Bref. Art books and graphic novels rather than souvenirs.

blocks.title: Bref · ceramics and independent design
blocks.text: Walk along Bernard to browse small-run ceramics, prints, and design objects. This is one of the shops to make time for.

nearby.text: Along Bernard: independent publishing, art books, and graphic novels. A browse-and-show-each-other-things stop with no booking.
Further east on Bernard: the sweet stop if bagels have worn off. Takeaway doughnuts; no reservation.

blocks.title: H Parfums · try something unfamiliar
blocks.text: Walk south toward Laurier and take your time with niche fragrances. Try a few on skin and let them develop while you walk.

nearby.text: On Saint-Laurent, east of the perfume boutique: wearable sculpture, experimental materials, and handmade art jewelry. An optional extra walk before lunch, or use it instead of a second perfume stop. Saturday 11 AM–5 PM.

blocks.title: Leméac · the nice lunch
blocks.text: Reserve a table for a proper French bistro lunch. Make this a long, seated meal rather than a sandwich eaten in a queue. Allow CAD 55–90 each before tax and tip, depending on drinks.
blocks.note: Weekend brunch/lunch is published as 10 AM–3 PM. Reserve.

nearby.text: If lunch runs long, this is the nearby fragrance browse to keep. Compare a few scents without adding another meal or reservation.

blocks.title: LVNEA · botanical perfume
blocks.text: Head east through the neighborhood to the Saint-Viateur boutique. Woods, resins, and atmospheric botanical scents made locally. Slow browsing is the activity.
blocks.note: Entrance on Casgrain. Published weekend hours 11 AM–6 PM.

nearby.text: A nearby workshop-boutique for locally made clothing, ceramics, jewelry, and other makers’ work. Browse on the way toward Saint-Laurent.
The art-jewelry option is south on Saint-Laurent, so browse before continuing north if this interests you more than another fragrance stop. Do not double back after chocolate.

blocks.title: État de choc · chocolate worth taking home
blocks.text: Walk north along Saint-Laurent to the chocolate specialist. Browse the bean-to-bar selection and pick out unusual bars or bonbons. This stays in Saturday’s northern shopping loop.

nearby.text: The workshop-boutique is along the Saint-Laurent part of today’s loop. Local clothing and makers’ objects, with ceramics and jewelry to browse.

A nearby dinner alternative with ambitious plated desserts and wine. It opens at 5 PM. Saturday 7:45 PM was listed for two when checked; using it after skating means a taxi back north. Book it instead of Monarque, not as a second dinner.

blocks.title: MONOKIINI · handmade ceramics and coffee
blocks.text: Continue north to the ceramics studio and café. Browse sculptural handmade cups and objects, see the making space, and sit with a coffee. This is the signature boutique stop in the northern loop.
blocks.note: A browse-and-coffee visit. Sip & Clay classes require separate booking and weeks of firing, so we are not building the day around a class.

nearby.text: Chocolate to take home on the way to the studio. A compact shopping stop if you want more time seated with coffee at MONOKIINI.

blocks.title: Hotel break · leave room for dinner
blocks.text: Taxi back to Alt Hotel Montréal in Griffintown, drop your purchases, and take a short break before skating. Walk or take a short taxi onward to Atrium Le 1000.

nearby.text: Chez Potier is on Wellington near your Griffintown hotel. An easy pastry stop if you want something sweet before skating; Sunday remains the planned longer visit.

blocks.title: Atrium Le 1000 · the skating anchor
blocks.text: Head to the indoor rink beneath the glass atrium. Select Saturday November 21, the 4:30–5:30 PM arrival window, and arrive around 5 PM. Skate for about an hour before dinner. The rink stays open until 9 PM.
blocks.note: The live calendar was checked November 18 and showed places in that arrival window. Nothing is booked. CAD 12 entry + CAD 10 skate rental + CAD 1 required helmet rental if needed. Rentals are on site. Outdoor Esplanade Tranquille opens November 25, after this trip.

nearby.text: A mansion-bar option downtown for cocktails and a snack before a later dinner. This is at Le Mount Stephen, a separate hotel from your Alt booking. Bar seats are walk-in.

blocks.title: Monarque · brasserie dinner
blocks.text: Monarque brasserie remains the preferred dinner: polished French food, a lively room, and à la carte ordering. Request a table for two around 7 PM. The live Saturday calendar currently shows no brasserie tables, so this is a target, not a confirmed plan.

nearby.text: An atmospheric walk before or after dinner: large projections on old-city walls. The operator lists nine reopened tableaux Wednesday–Sunday after dark. The Saint-Nicolas/Récollets area is near Monarque. Free; the optional app adds sound and context.
A nearby daytime café to remember for Sunday lunch, rather than an evening dinner backup. Sandwiches and pastry; check the queue before committing.

blocks.note: Checked November 18: the only displayed Saturday dinner slot was 9:30 PM in Salle à Manger, the more formal room with a different menu. Call +1 514 875-3896 for a brasserie cancellation or use the dinner shortlist below. If choosing 9:30 PM, have cocktails and a snack before dinner.

blocks.time: After dinner, or before a 9:30 PM dinner
blocks.title: Cloakroom · one excellent cocktail
blocks.text: Try Cloakroom for one cocktail tailored to the flavors you like. After a 7 PM dinner, aim around 9:15 PM. If you take Monarque’s 9:30 PM formal-room slot, move the cocktail to around 7 PM and taxi to dinner afterward.
blocks.note: Bar George is near Cloakroom if it is full. Both are downtown, so take a taxi back to Alt Hotel Montréal in Griffintown afterward.

nearby.text: Near Cloakroom: mansion-bar cocktails at Le Mount Stephen. This is a separate stop, not your hotel. Both cocktail bars are walk-in; taxi back to Alt afterward.

days.label: Sunday
days.title: Old Montréal at leisure. Fly home at 8 PM.
days.summary: A long café breakfast, artisan boutiques, the waterfront, Notre-Dame, and beautiful pastries. Collect bags at 3:45 PM and leave the hotel at 4 PM for your 8 PM flights.

blocks.title: Crew Collective & Café · breakfast under the bank ceiling
blocks.text: Check out and leave your bags with Alt Hotel Montréal, then walk or taxi into Old Montréal to Crew. Take a table for breakfast and coffee in the former Royal Bank hall. This is the morning’s long sit-down stop.

nearby.text: A second excellent daytime café toward the western end of Old Montréal. Better as a savory lunch swap later than a second full breakfast; walk-in and sometimes a queue.

blocks.title: Saint-Paul craft shops · L’Empreinte & WACHIYA
blocks.text: Walk the old streets to two artisan shops opposite one another: Québec ceramics, glass and jewelry at L’Empreinte, and Cree beadwork and handmade objects at WACHIYA.
blocks.note: Two independent craft boutiques on Saint-Paul East, across from one another. Take your time rather than treating them as quick stops.

nearby.text: Return to whichever maker’s work caught your eye: Québec ceramics, glass, and jewelry. Ask about the maker rather than rushing through a checklist.
Across the street: Cree beadwork and artisan objects from Eeyou Istchee. A different craft tradition from L’Empreinte, worth browsing as a pair.

blocks.title: Old Port · walk by the river
blocks.text: Stroll from Saint-Paul toward the waterfront and along the quays. Keep this as unstructured walking-and-talking time, then head back toward Place d’Armes. If it is cold or wet, spend longer in the shops and café instead.

nearby.text: Stay close to Saint-Paul East for a final artisan browse if the waterfront is too windy. No booking or transport needed.
The grand indoor café is the comfortable weather fallback. Go back for a warm drink rather than forcing an exposed waterfront walk.

blocks.title: Place d’Armes & Notre-Dame · the star sight
blocks.text: Walk through Place d’Armes and go inside Notre-Dame for the blue-and-gold interior. Allow a full hour to look around rather than squeezing it in before an airport run. Daytime admission starts at CAD 16 plus tax.
blocks.note: Sunday sightseeing is published as 12:30–4 PM. Choose a daytime ticket, separate from the evening AURA show.

nearby.text: Nearby on Saint-Jacques if you want another quiet coffee stop after the basilica. The architecture is part of the appeal, and there is no ticket to reserve.
Head west afterward for a seated sandwich lunch, then keep Chez Potier as the dessert stop. Choose this if you are hungry for more than pastry and a savory snack.

blocks.title: Chez Potier · a proper pastry afternoon
blocks.text: Walk west through the old streets to Wellington for refined pastries and something savory for a late light lunch. Choose the desserts that look best that day. There is time to enjoy them before heading back for your bags.

nearby.text: Olive et Gourmando is the nearby sit-down sandwich alternative. Use it instead of the savory part of lunch if seats and timing work.

blocks.note: Seating is limited. Olive et Gourmando is the nearby sit-down lunch option if you want a longer meal before the pastry stop.

blocks.title: Alt Hotel Montréal · collect bags
blocks.text: Return to Alt Hotel Montréal in Griffintown and collect your luggage. Chez Potier is near the hotel, so you can walk back after pastries. Have the airport taxi arranged for 4 PM.

blocks.title: Transfer to YUL · a proper airport buffer
blocks.text: Take a taxi to Montréal–Trudeau together. Allow an hour for the transfer and target YUL at 5 PM, three hours before both 8 PM departures. The hour is a planning allowance; check live traffic before pickup.

blocks.title: Two nonstop flights · same airport departure time
blocks.text: Milo: Air Canada AC736, YUL 8 PM → New York LaGuardia 9:30 PM. Forrest: Air Canada Express AC8612, YUL 8 PM → Boston 9:28 PM. Milo’s scheduled landing meets the 10 PM New York constraint. Boston landing at 9:28 PM leaves the trip home afterward, around your requested 10–11 PM window depending on your address and baggage.
blocks.note: Listed on Google Flights November 18 for Sunday November 22, 2026: LGA from USD 335 and BOS from USD 541, one way per person in economy with a carry-on. Fares and seats can change. Nothing is booked; scheduled arrival times are not guarantees.

practical.title: Book the anchors
practical.text: Hotel booked: Alt Hotel Montréal, 120 Rue Peel, Griffintown. Restaurant reservations, skating tickets, Notre-Dame admission, and flights remain pending unless booked separately. Tell reception you expect arrival after midnight on Friday night.

practical.title: Time to talk
practical.text: Saturday covers the northern shops once. Sunday stays in Old Montréal. MONOKIINI and skating are Saturday’s highlights; Notre-Dame is Sunday’s main sight. Nearby extras stay optional.

practical.title: Getting around
practical.text: Walk within each neighborhood and taxi between clusters. Alt Hotel Montréal in Griffintown is your booked base. Sunday pastries at Chez Potier are near the hotel, making luggage collection straightforward. Restaurant prices are CAD before tax and tip.

practical.title: Milo · New York return
practical.text: Sunday November 22: Air Canada AC736, YUL 8 PM → LGA 9:30 PM, nonstop. Listed from USD 335 one way with a carry-on when checked November 18. This meets the requirement to land in New York by 10 PM. Nothing is booked.

practical.title: Forrest · Boston return
practical.text: Sunday November 22: Air Canada Express AC8612, YUL 8 PM → BOS 9:28 PM, nonstop. Listed from USD 541 one way with a carry-on when checked November 18. Get home afterward; no need to cut Montréal short for an earlier Boston arrival. Nothing is booked.

practical.title: Sunday pickup
practical.text: Collect bags at 3:45 PM, leave Alt Hotel Montréal at 4 PM, and target YUL at 5 PM for the two 8 PM departures. Saturday remains the only northern shopping loop; skating stays Saturday.

practical.title: Airport recommendation
practical.text: YUL recommends arrival at least 3 hours before departure. The transfer hour is a planning allowance, not a traffic prediction. US immigration is handled at YUL before departure.

neighborhoods.name: Mile End & Outremont
neighborhoods.subtitle: Coffee, independent design, perfume, and a polished bistro. Your Saturday morning cluster.

neighborhoods.name: The Plateau
neighborhoods.subtitle: Lunch, handmade chocolates, a great pastry, and a short game of pinball. Walk between these stops.

neighborhoods.name: Old Montréal & the river
neighborhoods.subtitle: The main afternoon and Sunday cluster. Chez Potier is at the western edge; Habitat 67 needs a taxi across the water.

neighborhoods.name: Golden Square Mile
neighborhoods.subtitle: Two polished evening stops near the downtown hotels. A taxi transfer from Old Montréal.

neighborhoods.name: Little Italy · the dessert detour
neighborhoods.subtitle: North of Mile End, so treat this as a separate cluster. Ratafia is an evening destination; chocolate and shopping work in the day.

hotels.name: Le Germain Montréal
hotels.label: Easy default
hotels.description: Refined, comfortable, and central. The cleanest shared-room choice.

hotels.name: Hôtel William Gray
hotels.label: Best old-city atmosphere
hotels.description: Stone architecture, contemporary rooms, and a real hotel living room. Best if you want the hotel to feel part of the trip.
hotels.beds: Confirm a two-bed category; many rooms are kings.

hotels.name: Alt Hotel Montréal
hotels.label: Booked
hotels.description: Your booked base in Griffintown, at Peel and Wellington, near Chez Potier and the Lachine Canal.

hotels.name: Hôtel Nelligan
hotels.label: Warm, romantic old stone
hotels.description: Brick, beams, and a cozy Old Montréal base. A good counterpoint to the modern downtown hotels.
hotels.beds: Confirm the current two-bed room category directly.

reservations.name: Leméac · lunch for two
reservations.status: 12:30 PM displayed as available, checked Nov 18. Book this.

reservations.name: One dinner for two
reservations.status: Monarque brasserie is the first choice but has no displayed slots. See the checked alternatives below. Reserve only one dinner.

reservations.name: Atrium Le 1000 · skating
reservations.status: Select the 4:30–5:30 PM arrival window. Live calendar previously checked Nov 18; rent skates and the required helmet if needed.

reservations.name: Notre-Dame · daytime visit
reservations.status: Buy daytime admission for Sunday. Published sightseeing hours 12:30–4 PM; exact ticket inventory not checked.

reservations.name: Hotel · BOOKED
reservations.status: Alt Hotel Montréal, 120 Rue Peel, Griffintown. Booked by you; room category follows your confirmation. Notify reception of your after-midnight arrival.

dinner_options.text: First choice: the brasserie for à la carte French food and a lively, polished room. Target Saturday 7 PM for two. No brasserie slots displayed on Nov 18; call +1 514 875-3896 for cancellations. Resy showed 9:30 PM in Salle à Manger, the more formal room with a different menu. Choose that only if a late, longer dinner appeals.

Best dessert-focused alternative: inventive savory plates, plated desserts, wine, and an intimate Art Deco room. Saturday 7:45 PM and 8 PM were listed for two on Nov 18. It is in Little Italy near the afternoon shopping, so using it after skating requires another taxi north. This replaces Monarque.

Best grand-room option, at Le Mount Stephen downtown, separate from your Alt hotel: British-inspired food, beef Wellington, and elaborate desserts. Target Saturday 7 PM, but the live calendar showed no dining-room availability within three hours of that time. Ask the restaurant about cancellations. Cocktail bar seating is walk-in; a dinner booking does not reserve cocktail-only seats.

The classic Montréal bistro option: steak frites, tartare, an extensive cellar, and maple profiteroles. A less decorative, very established room. The Saturday calendar showed only midnight slots for two when checked, so it is a cancellation option rather than a sensible timed backup. Book online or call +1 514 845-5333.

cocktails: No cocktail reservation to make: Cloakroom accepts no reservations. Aim around 9:15 PM after a 7 PM dinner, or around 7 PM before a 9:30 PM Monarque dinner. Bar George’s bar seats are also walk-in. Both are subject to space.
